summary: ING's current-account pages are the clearest and most mobile-first in the measured set, but they also carry far more pressure and persuasion than the market: roughly four urgency or deadline markers against a peer average of 0.6, five persuasion techniques against 1.7, and a page about twice as long as peers. The strengths (offer clarity, mobile-first design, desire-building) are worth protecting, while the urgency, 'free'-with-conditions and fast-sign-up claims are the biggest credibility risks. Every point below is a hypothesis to test: the dataset contains no click, conversion or sales data, spans six product families and three languages, and rests on a single judge's scores.

recommendations.title: Strip back urgency and deadline language
recommendations.finding: ING uses about 4 urgency or deadline markers per page against a peer average of 0.6, a gap of 3.69 standard deviations and the single largest difference in the comparison; it is also one of the three signals that most distinguishes ING from the market.
recommendations.recommendation: On the current-account pages, remove countdown and deadline phrasing (closing dates, 'only until', 'last chance') and keep at most one time-bound element per page, tied to a real, verifiable end date.

recommendations.title: Reduce the number of persuasion techniques stacked per page
recommendations.finding: ING pages combine five persuasion techniques on average versus 1.67 for peers (3.68 standard deviations above), the second-largest gap measured; the effect size is a rubric judgment by a single rater, so treat the direction as reliable and the exact size as indicative.
recommendations.recommendation: Pick one persuasion lever per page (for example a clear product benefit or a social-proof element) and delete the rest, so the argument for opening the account is not diluted by stacked pressure tactics.

recommendations.title: Make the conditions behind 'free' explicit
recommendations.finding: In 0.67 of ING's pages a 'free' claim carries conditions, against 0.23 for peers; this is a model-assisted measure, so verify the flagged instances manually before rewriting.
recommendations.recommendation: Where a free account, card or transfer is claimed, state the qualifying conditions (minimum deposit, salary transfer, age or package requirement) directly next to the claim rather than only in the legal small print.

recommendations.title: Shorten the current-account page
recommendations.finding: ING pages measure about 11,100 pixels tall against a peer average of about 6,400, and carry 33 images against 19; length and image volume together make the page roughly twice the market norm.
recommendations.recommendation: Cut the page to the sections that carry the decision (offer, conditions, price, how to open) and move documentation, FAQ-style detail and secondary products to separate pages linked from the main one.

recommendations.title: Replace image volume with one strong opening visual
recommendations.finding: ING runs 33 images per page against a peer average of 19, while challenger pages put a much larger share of the page into a single opening image (0.62 against 0.25 at traditional banks) and show fewer elements above the fold (21.5 against 36.6).
recommendations.recommendation: Consolidate the image set into one dominant hero visual plus a small number of supporting visuals, and reduce the number of competing blocks visible before the first scroll so the opening screen has one clear focal point.

recommendations.title: Put a concrete price or rate on the page
recommendations.finding: None of the traditional bank pages in the set shows a rate, while half of the challenger pages do (0.5); ING's profile places it between the two groups, so a visible figure is a plausible point of differentiation rather than a break with its positioning.
recommendations.recommendation: Show the account's headline price signal (monthly fee, or the fee waived under stated conditions) as a plain figure near the top of the page instead of describing the offer only qualitatively.

recommendations.title: Substantiate the fast digital sign-up promise
recommendations.finding: ING claims fast digital sign-up on 0.67 of its pages against 0.15 for peers, but this is a model-assisted signal with a smaller gap (1.42 standard deviations) and the smallest evidence base of the gaps listed.
recommendations.recommendation: Back the promise with concrete, checkable detail on the page (number of steps, what the customer needs at hand, expected time to a usable account) or drop the speed claim where it cannot be supported.

recommendations.title: Protect the clarity and mobile-first strengths
recommendations.finding: ING scores 5.0 on offer clarity against a peer mean of 3.97, is designed mobile-first on every measured page (1.0 against 0.56) and makes the offer feel worth having on every page (1.0 against 0.59); these are the areas where it already leads.
recommendations.recommendation: Treat these as constraints on the changes above: any shortening or copy rewrite should keep one plainly stated value proposition and the mobile-first layout intact, and should be checked first on a phone-sized rendering.

recommendations.title: Test a calmer background against the current bright treatment
recommendations.finding: ING's pages measure 0.55 background luminance against a peer average of 0.34, brighter than both the traditional (0.43) and challenger (0.17) groups; brightness is measured on a single light-mode capture, so this describes our screenshot rather than every visitor's experience.
recommendations.recommendation: Run a page-level test of a lower-luminance background on one current-account page and compare engagement with the current treatment before rolling it out.

recommendations.title: Do not build campaign copy on digital-superiority claims
recommendations.finding: ING's 20 headlines in the last 90 days are about financial results (7), product launch (6), other (5), esg_sustainability (1) and regulatory (1), and none falls under an innovation_digital theme. That is context about what the press covers, not evidence about any page; the link to page wording is a hypothesis to verify.
recommendations.recommendation: On the open-account and youth pages, replace broad digital-leadership framing with concrete, checkable descriptions of what happens when someone opens the account, and align product messaging with the product-launch themes the press is actually covering.
recommendations.reputation_context: Drawn from ING's 90-day theme counts: financial_results 7, product_launch 6, esg_sustainability 1, regulatory 1, other 5, with no innovation_digital theme present. Hypothesis only; theme counts describe topics, not performance.

recommendations.title: Keep employment and earnings framing out of campaign copy
recommendations.finding: Several of ING's results headlines pair a profit figure of close to 1.9 billion euros with the announcement of 400 job cuts worldwide, and one reports a Dutch court barring ING from closing Gazprom's accounts. This is news context only and says nothing about how any page performed; any effect on page reception is a hypothesis to verify.
recommendations.recommendation: Review the current-account and open-account pages for copy that leans on savings or price framing in a way that could read oddly against that coverage, and keep the campaign text focused on the product itself rather than on the bank's scale or cost position.
recommendations.reputation_context: Drawn from ING's 20 headlines in the last 90 days and its financial_results theme count of 7, of which the notable headlines concern 400 job cuts announced alongside close to 1.9 billion euros of profit and the Gazprom court ruling.

recommendations.title: Avoid broad sustainability claims in the current-account copy
recommendations.finding: ING's themes include esg_sustainability with 1 headline, and that notable headline reports that ING is barely reducing fossil financing. That is a topic count, not a sentiment measure, and it is not evidence about any page; the recommendation is a hypothesis to verify.
recommendations.recommendation: Keep any environmental mention on the campaign pages narrow and factual — tied to a specific, verifiable product or scheme — rather than using general green framing that could be read against that coverage.
recommendations.reputation_context: Drawn from ING's esg_sustainability theme count of 1 among 20 headlines in the last 90 days, whose notable headline concerns ING's fossil financing record.
